text:
Labor’s New South Wales leadership has been accused of alienating members and undermining the democratic process, after multiple state election candidates were preselected by “captain’s call” instead of the rank and file.
The premier, Chris Minns, announced on Friday that commercial litigator Jade Tyrrell will be Labor’s candidate for the marginal Liberal-held seat of Lane Cove at March’s state election.
He confirmed the nomination is the latest to be sent to Labor’s national executive, a procedure which bypasses a preselection by branch members.
Guardian Australia understands that Labor’s candidate at the 2023 election, Ryde councillor Penny Pedersen – who reduced the margin of the previously safe Liberal seat by almost two-thirds – was asked not to nominate by Labor head office, in favour of another candidate, Vivienne Moxham-Hall, a former adviser to the health minister, Ryan Park.
After Moxham-Hall – who was subsequently endorsed by local members – withdrew her nomination this month, citing a change in her current workplace policy, Tyrrell has become the second candidate to be chosen for the electorate by party leadership.
A local Labor source said Moxham-Hall and Tyrrell were both highly qualified candidates, but local rank-and-file members had been “strung along” by head office.
“We’ve been trying to win this seat since 2011 and the first time we get close they say all of a sudden, ‘No, we’re imposing a different candidate,’” they said.
In recent weeks, Minns and the party’s organisational wing in Sussex Street have faced accusations of making “captain’s calls” on candidates in multiple winnable or Labor-held seats.
This includes the premier publicly endorsing candidates in seats without rank-and-file preselections, in some cases before the national executive had signed off on them. The candidates in 12 seats for March’s election have been sent to the national executive so far.
Under Labor party rules, the 21-member executive, which includes prime minister Anthony Albanese, can intervene over rank-and-file preselections to choose candidates. While other candidates can still nominate, a recommendation by NSW party leadership in one candidate’s favour is considered a fait accompli.
In the safe Liberal seat of Epping, the premier last week endorsed former Liberal staffer and councillor Tanya Raffoul as Labor’s candidate, a move which has drawn some internal anger.
Although another Labor member Benson Koschinski nominated against Raffoul, the national executive endorsed Raffoul’s candidacy in a unanimous vote.
Guardian Australia understands every member of the executive subbed out to allow proxy voters. NSW minister Rose Jackson subbed in for Albanese, while other proxies included staffers from the premier’s and senior NSW ministers’ offices.
One senior Labor source, speaking on the condition of anonymity to discuss internal matters, said it was not unusual for proxies to be used when ballots were conducted on short notice, but others said it was highly unusual for every single member to nominate one.
Multiple senior branch sources said sending preselections to the national executive had become too regular.
One said it had become “the norm instead of the extraordinary”, while another said it was undermining Labor institutions.
“How does this help the health of the party?” they said.
‘Not running a charity’
In Terrigal, another marginal Liberal seat – and the only one held by the Coalition on the central coast – the deputy premier, Prue Car, on Thursday announced local high school principal Lisa Wicks as Labor’s candidate.
The party’s candidate in 2023, Sam Boughton, had been re-endorsed by members but recently dropped out following a family tragedy and has endorsed Wicks.
Guardian Australia understands that Wicks was first introduced to members at a branch meeting as a new member of the party on Sunday.
In a meeting with members at another local branch on Wednesday – the evening before the announcement – a senior member of Labor’s organisational wing said Wicks would be the party’s candidate after the preselection had been sent to the national executive without any other nominations.
One local member said some at the meeting accepted this, but others supported a preselection “in order for the rank and file to be given their say, after which we would probably have been satisfied with who had been chosen democratically, as is our right”.
A senior Labor party source said the unforeseen circumstances which led to candidates dropping out in Lane Cove and Terrigal had made the use of the national executive necessary.
On Tuesday, Minns said the preselection for Rockdale, a seat held by the sports minister, Steve Kamper, who is a close political ally, would be decided by the executive, following a similar announcement last week about another sitting minister Anoulack Chanthivong.
The intervention in Rockdale has drawn criticism from the former Labor upper house member Shaoquett Moselmane, who said he would have nominated for a rank and file preselection.
“Such action represents yet another example of a party leadership that is increasingly detached from the needs and aspirations of the majority of party members,” he said.
“It’s an act of trampling over party principles of fairness, transparency and honesty in preselection.”
Speaking alongside Tyrrell on Friday, Minns said he understood “concern and consternation about some of those processes”, but cited the threat posed by One Nation which is consistently polling a close second to Labor in NSW.
“I have to put the best team on the path, I have to put outstanding candidates, ones that have got deep connections with the local community, an element of the community that have traditionally voted maybe for a conservative candidate” he said.
Tyrrell, a Labor party member of 15 years, said she had grown up in Hunters Hill, which is in the Lane Cove electorate, and now lived in Waverton, which is in the neighbouring electorate of North Shore.
Guardian Australia understands Pedersen had been involved in monthly street stalls after the 2025 federal election success of local Labor member, Jerome Laxale, but that the party head office had asked for this campaigning to pause earlier this year.
In response to a series of detailed questions sent to NSW Labor head office and the premier, Guardian Australia was referred to comments Minns made at press conferences endorsing the candidates for Winston Hills and Wallsend, both preselections sent to the national executive.
Minns told reporters in Wallsend that Labor was “not running a charity” but a political party.
A Sussex Street source said if the candidates sent to the national executive were elected in March, there would be a “massive injection of talent in Macquarie Street”, including potential future ministers.
Pedersen and Moxham-Hall have been contacted for comment.
digest_he:
הנהגת מפלגת הלייבור בניו סאות' וויילס סופגת ביקורת חריפה מצד חברי מפלגה ובכירים מקומיים בטענה שהיא מערערת את התהליך הדמוקרטי ועוקפת את בחירת חברי הסניפים בבחירת מועמדים לבחירות המדינה. הביקורת מגיעה בעקבות שורה של החלטות שבהן בחרה הנהגת המפלגה להעביר מועמדים ישירות לאישור ההנהגה הלאומית במקום לקיים בחירות מקומיות.

דוגמאות בולטות כוללות את ההכרזה על מועמדים במושבים מתנדנדים ובטוחים כמו ליין קוב, אפינג ורוקדייל, כאשר במספר מקרים נתבקשו מועמדים קודמים או נבחרים מקומיים לפנות את מקומם לטובת מועמדים שזכו לגיבוי ישיר מצד ראש הממשלה המקומי כריס מינס וההנהגה. חברי מפלגה טוענים כי התנהלות זו פוגעת בעקרונות הבסיסיים של הוגנות ושקיפות, ומנתקת את ההנהגה מהשטח.

מצדם, מקורבים להנהגה ולראש הממשלה הגנו על המהלך בטענה שמדובר בצעד הכרחי המונע מאילוצים פוליטיים ומאיומים מצד מפלגות מתחרות כמו וואן ניישן, ומחייב הצבת צוות חזק ומוכר בקהילות המקומיות לקראת ההתמודדות הקרובה.
